properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean foundation composed of Carboniferous sedimentary sequences (Gullane Formation sandstones and shales) overlying volcanic dolerite sills and basaltic bedrock of the Edinburgh central volcanic complex. Superstructure masonry comprises fine-grained, silica-cemented pale buff-grey Craigleith sandstone ashlar and Hailes/Ravelston sandstone rubble backing, bonded with non-hydraulic lime and sharp sand mortar. The monument plinth incorporates polished grey and pink Peterhead granite blocks.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Mature urban parkland specimens within Charlotte Square Gardens: *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore), *Ulmus glabra* (Wych elm), and *Tilia cordata* (Small-leaved lime). Late September phenology: dense broadleaf canopies exhibiting early autumn chlorosis (mottled yellowing and pale olive-brown margins) with localized crown thinning and early leaf senescence.

properties.architectural_summary:
Neoclassical civic and Georgian residential square ensemble:
- Central background: West Register House (former St George's Church, Robert Reid, 1811–1814) featuring a monumental Greek-cross central block, tetrastyle portico, square clock-tower attic, cylindrical peristyle drum with Corinthian pilasters, and a massive copper-clad ribbed dome terminating in an octagonal stone lantern and gilded cross.
- Flanking wings: Robert Adam-designed neoclassical terraced townhouses (3 storeys over rusticated basements with attic dormers), channelled rustication to ground floor, polished ashlar upper floors, ionic pilastered end/centre bays, 6-over-6 and 12-pane timber sash-and-case fenestration, and pitched Scottish slate roofs with regular stone ashlar chimney stacks.
- Foreground: Prince Albert Memorial (Sir John Steell, 1876), stepped stepped granite pedestal surmounted by a bronze equestrian statue flanked by bronze corner sculptural groupings. All facade planes and vertical colonnade lines plumbed to true gravity vertical.
